why: EGM behaviour can change under a passing suite when a dependency moves. These are the revisions every measurement in this repository was taken against. A run record cites them; the runbook checks them before a validation run against a real machine. libsas is re-pinned whenever its version increases.

libsas.measured: Measured on 2026-11-05 against the demo built with QSP 2.3.6.32 (pull request 815) and QPM2 v9.0.0.13, on a demo started seconds before the run, with the layout-19 secure-enhanced memory. The 13 hand pay cases: 7 pass, 0 fail, 6 skip, against 3 pass, 4 fail, 6 skip on 2026-11-04 with v5.4.6.13. The four that now pass (3.5.2, 3.16, 3.18, 3.20) read long poll 1B as zeros after its hand pay reading is acknowledged, which is libsas #258. The six skips need capabilities the demo does not declare. On the same demo the full M7 tree gave 42 pass, 1 fail (4.12, which passed in the four runs after it), 138 skip, and the regression tree on the golden memory 18 pass, 18 fail, 14 skip; the two new failures were long poll 1F reporting a maximum bet of 0 and a base percentage of '0' padded with NULs, because long poll 56 reported no game enabled on the layout-19 memories. On 2026-11-05 the fixtures were rewritten with their games switched on; on them long poll 56 lists games 1 to 4, and long poll 1F reports a maximum bet of FF and '9211'. That run also had every note returned, but two other QSP platforms were running on the machine beside the demo, so its money cases are not a measurement.
libsas.howItIsHeld: QSP declares libsas as FetchContent 'sas' (v5.4.6.13 in pull request 815), and that declaration is not ours to edit. The preset SasWorkbenchM0-QSP815 overrides it with FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SAS, pointing the build at a clone held at this commit, C:/work/libsas-5.4.6.14, because the checkout at C:/Progetti/libsas is moved between branches by other work.

qsp.describedAs: QSP 2.3.6.32, pull request 815, open and untagged
qsp.howItIsHeld: The demo still declares QSP v2.3.6.1, and its CMakeLists is not ours to edit. The gitignored preset SasWorkbenchM0-QSP815 inherits SasWorkbenchM0 and sets FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_QSP to a separate clone at C:/work/qsp-pr815, checked out at this commit. It builds into out/build/SasWorkbenchM0-QSP815 and bin/SasWorkbenchM0-QSP815.

qpm2.howItIsHeld: Declared by QSP pull request 815 and fetched as released. Its simulated acceptor reports tickets, so the M0 preset does not override it.

qpmSimulator.howItIsHeld: The version QSP pull request 815 declares. SASWB_QPM_SIMULATOR_ROOT in the M0 preset points at the checkout at C:/Progetti/qpm_simulator, whose ticket encoder and wallet the substituted printer compiles in.

nvramArrangement.note: QSP 2.3.6.32 (pull request 815) writes NVRAM layout 19. The committed fixtures were configured by hand on 2026-11-05: an attendant NVRAM reset, then maker QX, address 1 on channel 1, asset 1, note acceptor 102, printer 101, standard validation, no ticket-in, and game denominations of 5, 10, 50 and 100 cents. After a reset the demo raises vendor condition 1 (licence key, 'Custom Condition 1') itself, which keeps the bill acceptor off, so it was cleared on the Licence Key audit page before saving. The accounting denomination of five cents was written with 'sasctl nvram denomination 0.05', and the secure-enhanced memory was written from the golden one. The configuration block is still at 0x000A00, and the host-link block moved from 0x00FF1E to 0x00FF22. The machine reported code $02 on long poll 1F. That build gives a newly chosen denomination its own enable record, switched off, so every game was saved disabled; 'sasctl nvram games enable' switched on each denomination the five-cent unit divides, and the memory as saved by hand is kept in fixtures/nvram/arrangement-19-as-saved. The game records sit at 0x01034E, 0x954 apart, measured on the simulator only. The layout-15 fixtures for a QSP v2.3.6.1 demo are kept in fixtures/nvram/arrangement-15, and the arrangement-7 ones in fixtures/nvram/arrangement-7.
